Call a foreign function

Source: R/ffi.R
ffi_call.Rd

Port of jax.ffi.ffi_call. Returns a function that calls the XLA FFI target target_name (registered with ffi_register_target()). Its unnamed arguments are the input arrays and its named arguments are the attributes of the handler. It works eagerly and under jit() and vmap() (see vmap_method); it cannot be differentiated (use custom_jvp() or custom_vjp()).

Usage

ffi_call(
  target_name,
  result_shape_dtypes,
  has_side_effect = FALSE,
  vmap_method = NULL,
  input_layouts = NULL,
  output_layouts = NULL,
  input_output_aliases = NULL,
  custom_call_api_version = 4L,
  legacy_backend_config = NULL
)

Arguments

target_name

The name of the registered target.

result_shape_dtypes

A ShapeDtypeStruct() (or array) describing the output, or a list of them for several outputs (the function then returns a list).

has_side_effect

Whether the call has side effects: it then runs even when its outputs are unused.

vmap_method

How the call behaves under vmap(), as for pure_callback(): "sequential", "sequential_unrolled", "expand_dims", "broadcast_all", "legacy_vectorized" or NULL (vmap is then an error).

input_layouts, output_layouts

NULL (row major), or a list with one entry per input (output): NULL or a major to minor order of the axes (0-based, so c(1, 0) is a column major matrix).

input_output_aliases

NULL, or a named integer vector or list mapping input indices (names) to output indices, 0-based: the output reuses the buffer of the input.

custom_call_api_version

The custom call API of the target; 4 (the default) is the typed FFI.

legacy_backend_config

For custom_call_api_version < 4: the opaque backend configuration string.

Value

A function of the inputs and attributes.

Details

Attributes convert as in JAX: an R integer scalar is a 64-bit integer (a Python int), a double scalar a 64-bit float, a logical scalar a boolean, a string a string, a jax scalar an attribute of its dtype, a jax array or an R vector of length other than one a dense array (of int64 for R integers, as for Python integers, and float64 for R doubles; pass a jax array for another dtype), a named list a dictionary and an unnamed list an array of attributes.

See also

ffi_register_target()
